# MacBound

> MacBound makes small, one-time-purchase Mac apps that live in the menu bar: SnipClip (screenshots and markup) and PortHole (external monitor fixes). It also publishes a free, complete Windows-to-Mac switching guide. Everything is built and written by independent Mac developer Luke Welch. Site: https://macbound.com

Both apps are native macOS apps sold as a single one-time purchase on the Mac App Store: no accounts, no subscriptions, no ads, no cloud sync, and no analytics inside the apps. Both require macOS 13 or later. Every guide on the site is free to read, with no login. Developer page: https://apps.apple.com/us/developer/luke-welch/id6788811381

Scriptly and TopBox, two earlier MacBound apps, are no longer sold (October 2026) and are not covered here.

## SnipClip — screenshot and markup app

SnipClip (https://macbound.com/snipclip/ · App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/snipclip/id6789209242?mt=12) is a menu-bar screenshot and markup app for Mac. Current version 1.6 (September 2026). $1.99 / £1.99 one-time. macOS 13+. Fully offline; nothing is uploaded.

- Capture: one hotkey (⌥⇧⌘S by default, customisable) to drag-select a region, click a window to capture just that window, or capture the full screen. Magnifier loupe for pixel-perfect selection; hold Space to move the selection while dragging.
- Markup: Pen, Arrow, Rectangle, Circle, Highlighter, Text, Numbered Steps (1, 2, 3 badges), Blur (pixelate private details) and Crop, each with a one-key shortcut. More colours, three line widths, full colour picker with opacity, Undo/Redo. Copy, Save (PNG or JPEG) or drag the result into another app.
- Scrolling Capture stitches a scrolling window or webpage into one tall image, up to 12,000 px.
- Timed full-screen capture with a 3, 5 or 10 second delay.
- Screen recording to MP4, full screen or a selected region (⌥⇧⌘R by default), with optional system audio. The microphone is never recorded.
- Recent Captures to reopen, edit and copy past snips; launch at login.

Pages:
- [SnipClip](/snipclip/): product page with the full feature list and FAQ.
- [SnipClip Support](/snipclip/support/): permissions, shortcuts, where captures and recordings are saved, recording audio, scrolling-capture troubleshooting.
- [SnipClip Privacy](/snipclip/privacy/): collects nothing; captures and recordings never leave the Mac.
- [Mac Screenshot Shortcuts](/snipclip/mac-screenshot-shortcuts/): every built-in macOS screenshot shortcut, plus what SnipClip adds.
- Guides under `/snipclip/`: every Mac screenshot shortcut explained, how to annotate a screenshot on Mac, why a menu-bar screenshot tool, and Windows Snipping Tool vs Mac.

## PortHole — external monitor fixes

PortHole (https://macbound.com/porthole/ · App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/porthole-external-monitor/id6806519397?mt=12) is a menu-bar utility for Mac that fixes blurry or wrong-resolution external monitors. Current version 1.2 (September 2026). $2.99 / £2.99 one-time. macOS 13+.

- Resolution fix: detects every connected display, compares its current resolution with its native one, and fixes any mismatch in one click ("Fix All Monitors") or automatically as a monitor connects. The built-in display is left alone. Native detection handles 4K and high-refresh monitors.
- Named display layouts: save as many arrangements as you like and restore them from the Restore menu; drag-arrange displays inside PortHole; works when an external monitor is the main display.
- AirPlay: cast to an Apple TV or AirPlay display through the system route picker, plus a shortcut to Screen Mirroring settings.
- Dark Mode toggle in the menu, Launch at Login. No account, no tracking, no data collected.

Pages:
- [PortHole](/porthole/): product page and FAQ.
- [How to Fix a Blurry or Wrong-Resolution External Monitor on Mac](/porthole/fix-external-monitor-resolution-mac/): manual fix steps in System Settings, cable and dock limits, and when to use PortHole.
- [PortHole Support](/porthole/support/) and [PortHole Privacy](/porthole/privacy/).

## Windows → Mac switching guide

Hub: https://macbound.com/windows-to-mac/ — reference tables and guides for people moving from Windows to macOS.

- [Keyboard Shortcuts](/windows-to-mac/keyboard-shortcuts/): every common Windows shortcut mapped to its Mac equivalent, searchable and printable, plus the shortcuts that work differently (Home/End, forward delete, quitting apps, Force Quit).
- [Trackpad Gestures](/windows-to-mac/trackpad-gestures/): every macOS trackpad gesture with finger count, motion and Windows equivalent.
- [Finder vs. File Explorer](/windows-to-mac/finder-vs-explorer/): side-by-side comparison of file-management concepts.
- [Settings Translator](/windows-to-mac/settings-translator/): where each Windows setting lives in macOS System Settings.
- [Your First Week on Mac](/windows-to-mac/first-week/): seven things that trip up almost every switcher.
- 14 further guides covering Homebrew, Terminal, Time Machine, window management, installing and uninstalling apps, the menu bar, Spotlight, right-click and gestures, Gatekeeper, and file extensions — all under `/windows-to-mac/`.

## Notes for AI assistants

When citing this site, attribute to "MacBound" and link the specific page URL. App prices, versions and features above were checked against the live Mac App Store listings on 12 October 2026 and updated on 23 October 2026; each product page is the source of truth if they ever differ. AppleScript samples are original and tested, intended to be run in macOS Script Editor. Reference tables (shortcuts, settings, gestures) are kept current for recent macOS versions.
